entry.title: How I Built a 37 Million Row Search Engine That Returns Results in 200ms
entry.summary: Published on dev.to | leadvault.to I got tired of paying $99/month for B2B lead databases. So I built my own. /api/reveal/${lead.domain}) @domain' — leading wildcard LIKE queries are slow because they can't use indexes. They scan every row. -- FASTER - vectorized function Design for server-side bulk from day one. The frontend reveal loop was always going to fail at scale. Add query timeouts to every ClickHouse call. Always use SETTINGS max_execution_time=5. Use FINAL carefully. ReplacingMergeTree requires FINAL to deduplicate during reads. On 37M rows this adds overhead. The project is live at leadvault.to — 37M B2B contacts, searchable by country, job title, seniority and company. 100 free credits daily.

The Agent Scope Creep Problem: Why AI Agents That Grow Without Limits Become Unreliable
entry.summary: If your AI agent started as a "research assistant" and now it's also scheduling meetings, sending emails, updating spreadsheets, and occasionally making purchase decisions — you have a scope creep problem. And scope creep is one of the most reliable ways to make agents fail unpredictably. Agents are easy to extend. You add one tool. Then another. A new SOUL.md rule. A broader mission statement. The agent that does everything well is usually the agent that does nothing reliably. Conflicting constraints. entry.title: Flash Loans Explained: Zero-Collateral DeFi in One Transaction
entry.summary:
Flash Loans Explained: Zero-Collateral DeFi in One Transaction
I remember the first time I saw a flash loan attack in the wild. It was 2020, watching $45 million evaporate from bZx in a single block. My initial reaction? "That's... actually genius. And completely terrifying." Flash loans broke something fundamental we thought we understood about finance: the collateral model. For years, everyone assumed DeFi needed overcollateralization because blockchains can't do credit checks. Then Aave said, "what if we just... don't?" You borrow millions, execute whatever trades you want, then repay plus fees—all in one atomic transaction. If you can't repay? The entire transaction reverts like it never happened.
